 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. NEWCASTLE UNITED VS EVERTON 
 Premier League | Monday 2nd November 2026 | 8:00pm | St James' Park 
 Newcastle United have an opportunity to put things right on Monday night, but the pressure is firmly on Matthias Jaissle and his players to deliver a response after a disappointing midweek defeat against Everton.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Magpies welcome David Moyes' side to St James' Park for the second meeting between the clubs in just five days, with revenge very much on the agenda following Everton's 3-1 victory in the Carabao Cup fourth round.
 For Newcastle, this is about considerably more than simply putting a cup defeat behind them. It is about restoring confidence, responding to criticism and giving the supporters something to get behind after an inconsistent opening to the Premier League campaign.
 The manner of Thursday night's defeat will undoubtedly have frustrated supporters. Newcastle found themselves three goals behind after James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry all found the net, with Dan Burn's late consolation doing little to change the outcome.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It was another concerning performance from a Newcastle side that continues to struggle with consistency under Jaissle. While there have been encouraging moments, particularly the recent 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace, the Magpies have struggled to build any meaningful momentum.
 Monday provides an immediate opportunity to change that narrative.
 A RESPONSE IS REQUIRED 
 Newcastle currently find themselves in the middle of a frustrating period, with defensive vulnerabilities and a lack of consistency becoming increasingly noticeable.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Despite having plenty of attacking quality within the squad, the Magpies have struggled to turn performances into results on a regular basis.
 Their defensive record is particularly concerning, having conceded 14 goals in their opening eight Premier League matches. That is an area Jaissle desperately needs to address if Newcastle are going to challenge for European qualification this season.
 St James' Park should provide the perfect environment for a response, but home advantage has not necessarily been the guarantee of success supporters have come to expect.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Only one of Newcastle's opening four Premier League home fixtures this season has ended in victory, while defensive mistakes have continued to undermine their attacking efforts.
 The supporters will want to see a much more aggressive, organised and determined Newcastle side on Monday evening.
 EVERTON ARRIVE WITH CONFIDENCE 
 Everton will travel to Tyneside knowing they have already demonstrated that they can cause Newcastle significant problems.
 Moyes' side have now won three of their last four meetings with the Magpies, including Thursday's Carabao Cup success.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Hayden Hackney was particularly impressive in that victory, registering a goal and an assist, while Thierno Barry once again demonstrated the threat he can pose against Newcastle.
 However, Everton have their own Premier League problems to address.
 Despite making a relatively positive start to the campaign, consecutive league defeats against Chelsea and Arsenal have slowed their progress. They are also still searching for their first away victory in the Premier League this season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That provides Newcastle with an opportunity to take advantage, although the visitors will undoubtedly arrive believing they can secure another positive result.
 TEAM NEWS AND SELECTION QUESTIONS 
 Jaissle has several decisions to make when selecting his starting eleven.
 Will Osula is a doubt after suffering an ankle injury during Thursday's defeat, potentially opening the door for Yoane Wissa to lead the attack.
 Anthony Elanga has also returned to involvement following his hamstring injury and will be pushing for a starting position.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lewis Miley and Matias Fernandez-Pardo are also doubts, while Tino Livramento and goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen remain unavailable.
 There could be changes elsewhere, particularly in midfield, where Newcastle need greater physicality, energy and control.
 Joelinton could be an important inclusion, while Joe Willock will also be hoping to make an impression if given another opportunity.
 For Everton , Jarrad Branthwaite is expected to be available after following concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish's situation remains uncertain following his disciplinary omission.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A HUGE NIGHT FOR JAISSLE 
 There is no escaping the fact that pressure is beginning to build around Newcastle's head coach.
 Supporters want to see evidence that his methods are working and that the squad is moving in the right direction.
 A convincing performance against Everton would go some way towards restoring confidence, particularly after the disappointment of the Carabao Cup exit.
 However, another defeat would raise further questions about the direction of the team, the tactical approach and whether Jaissle can get the best out of the players at his disposal.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Newcastle cannot afford to allow Thursday's defeat to become another defining moment in an increasingly frustrating start to the season.
 THE VERDICT 
 Monday night's fixture feels like an important moment in Newcastle's campaign.
 The Magpies have the opportunity to respond in front of their own supporters, move further away from the disappointment of their cup elimination and put three valuable Premier League points on the board.
 Everton have already shown their capabilities, and Newcastle will need to be considerably better defensively if they are to avoid another frustrating evening.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The supporters will demand intensity, commitment and, above all, a performance that demonstrates this team still has the ambition and quality to compete.
 This is a revenge mission for Newcastle United .
 Three points would provide a much-needed boost for Jaissle and his players. Anything less, particularly another defeat, would leave even more questions hanging over St James' Park.
